summary: Dell Latitude 7440 provisioning hangs during post-enrolment when driverstore contains duplicate Broadcom NIC package
description: Issue summary: New hires' Dell Latitude 7440 devices consistently stall at the 'Completing device setup' stage immediately after Intune enrolment. Impact: Blocks first-login provisioning for ~20 new hires since 2026-03-08; requires manual intervention by IT imaging to complete setup. Environment: prod-us-west, standard corporate provisioning image (corp-win11-2026-02), Intune autopilot + SCCM hybrid co-management. Observed behaviour: device shows 'Provisioning stuck: Completing device setup' UI and Network driver does not initialize (no NIC). BitLocker auto-encrypt attempted but fails intermittently. No obvious SCCM task sequence errors; Intune shows device as Enrolled but Managed, and MDM enrollment logs show extended timeouts during device join.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Build Dell Latitude 7440 from imaging pool using corp-win11-2026-02 image. 2) Boot to OOBE and autopilot enroll to Intune. 3) Allow autopilot to run default provisioning (install corp apps, drivers via WinGet and Win10Drv packages). 4) Observe that after 'Completing device setup' the NIC remains in Device Manager with error code 31 or 28 and provisioning does not progress. 5) Manually inspect C:\Windows\INF and driver store. Note duplicate Broadcom NIC packages referenced in setupapi logs.
logs:
Most useful log excerpts below (timestamps in PST):

2026-03-09 08:22:34 PkgManager: Applying driver package Broadcom_NET_20.10.123.inf to device {GUID} -> STATUS_SUCCESS
2026-03-09 08:22:34 DriverFrameworks: Installing filter driver "bcmagent" returned code 0x0
2026-03-09 08:24:01 SetupAPI: Device Install failed for PCI\VEN_14E4&DEV_16B1, error 0x31 (a device attached to the system is not functioning)
2026-03-09 08:24:02 IntuneDisco: AutopilotTimeout during post-enroll (300s) -> retrying
2026-03-09 08:29:10 BITLOCKER: Auto-provision attempted; TPM ownership not found, aborting auto-encrypt

Full logs attached to ticket in the secure artifact store: s3://redwood-support-internal/prov-logs/INT-24999/
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Initial triage by Ava Patel: reproduces on 3/3 new devices from the spare pool. Hypothesis: duplicate driver packages in driverstore cause driver install race and leave NIC uninitialized.

2026-03-10 11:34 - Imaging team (Marco Ruiz): Confirmed duplicate Broadcom packages present; one package signature older (OEM-signed) and another packaged by WinGet installer. setupapi.log shows OS chooses older package but driver files mismatch -> code 31.
2026-03-10 13:00 - Network team: Verified firmware up-to-date on affected units; not a firmware regression. Confirmed identical symptoms when network driver pushed via SCCM packages or WinGet.

2026-03-11 08:45 - Hypothesis refined: SCCM hybrid driver deployment and WinGet driver bundle both present in provisioning recipe; when either runs before the other we see corrupt driverstore state. Intune's post-enroll timing magnifies race conditions.

2026-03-11 12:10 - Reproduced lab run with verbose setupapi logs; created script to enumerate driverstore: pnputil /enum-drivers shows two entries for Broadcom NetXtreme. Driver store path collision leads to SetupAPI selecting wrong INF copy.
comments: Ava Patel (2026-03-10 09:20): Added two repro devices to spare pool and captured setupapi.log and Intune enrollment trace. Putting artifacts in ticket S3 path. Notifying imaging team.

Marco Ruiz (Imaging) (2026-03-10 11:40): Looked at driverstore; confirmed duplicate Broadcom packages. Temporarily fixed by removing older OEM package from driverstore and re-running provisioning -> device completes. Creating a repro script.
Riley Chen (Network) (2026-03-10 14:05): From network side, not seeing hardware failure. Recommend we avoid pushing Broadcom driver via WinGet until imaging recipe is fixed.

Ava Patel (2026-03-11 09:00): Workaround rollout: updated spare-pool SOP to purge duplicate Broadcom entries before autopilot. Communicated to IT onboarding channel. 5 devices re-provisioned successfully.

Marco Ruiz (2026-03-11 17:30): Created draft PR to imaging-scripts to add a pre-sysprep driverstore cleanup step: https://github.com/redwood-inference/imaging-scripts/pull/412. Requesting review from platform infra.
Ava Patel (2026-03-12 08:15): Noted two customer hires still blocked yesterday; manual remediation applied. ETA to close after PR merged and one full-day staging rollout confirmed.
resolution: Workaround applied: manual purge of duplicate Broadcom driver packages from driverstore on affected devices, then reprovisioned. Persistent fix in progress via imaging-scripts PR that adds deterministic driverstore cleanup before WinGet/SCCM driver installs.
resolution_notes: 1) Merged PR to add 'driverstore purge' step to imaging pipeline (pending scheduled rollout). 2) Short-term SOP updated to include driverstore audit for Broadcom entries for spare pool devices. 3) Follow-up ticket to add telemetry alert when setupapi.log shows repeated INF collisions (INT-25001). 4) Recommend imaging recipe change: only one canonical source for NIC drivers (SCCM or WinGet), not both.
follow_up_actions: Imaging team to schedule staged rollout of PR in staging on 2026-03-14
Create INT-25001 to track setupapi INF collision telemetry and alerting
Update onboarding KB with manual purge steps
estimated_customer_impact: Internal hires onboarding delayed; roughly 20 devices impacted this week; average manual remediation time ~45 minutes per device.
